commentary_title: Pacific weakness and Atlantic oversupply driver rates decline in Capesize market
commentary_summary: The Capesize vessel utilisation fell WoW in tandem with falling tonne-miles index in week 41, while the Baltic benchmark C5TC rates also declined to $35,860/day. The market remained under pressure as limited cargo and ample vessel availability outweighed increased fixing activity along with, the Singapore public holiday and weaker FFA sentiment. | The C2 spot rates also declined to around $16.23/tonne, from $18.26/tonne the previous week, as available tonnage outpaced demand for early-October loading dates. Despite active fixing and elevated bunker costs at Chinese ports, owners competed aggressively for cargoes. | The South Atlantic remained under pressure, amid growing vessel availability and demand shifting towards November dates. The North Atlantic also softened despite fresh transatlantic and fronthaul enquiries.
